extracted.intended_audience: energy lawyers, regulators, NERC/FERC staff, and industry stakeholders involved in bulk-power system reliability standards
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluative and procedural criteria used by FERC and NERC for developing, approving, remanding, retiring, and enforcing Reliability Standards under FPA section 215, including substantive content expectations (e.g., cold-weather, inverter-based resources) and procedural deadlines/processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: ERO performance assessment timing
rubrics_metrics.description: ERO must submit to FERC a performance assessment three years from the date of certification as the ERO and every five years thereafter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reference to 18 C.F.R. § 39.3(c); procedural timing requirement for oversight and evaluation of ERO performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness in developing new or modified Reliability Standards
rubrics_metrics.description: NERC should develop most standards within twelve months and more complicated matters within fifteen months; FERC expects timely development in response to directives and expressed concern when actual averages (e.g., ~21.7 months) are significantly longer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FERC viewed slow responses (e.g., only ~15% of Order No. 693 directives addressed after three years) as evidence of inadequate ability to timely develop standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: FERC authority to direct standards development (FPA §215(d)(5))
rubrics_metrics.description: FERC has authority to direct the ERO to develop a new or modified Reliability Standard pursuant to FPA section 215(d)(5).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When FERC issues a directive under §215(d)(5), the ERO must affirmatively respond (not merely consider) and may propose alternative approaches that are equally efficient and effective; FERC does not intend to prescribe the precise text of standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: ERO affirmative obligation to respond to directives
rubrics_metrics.description: In response to a directive pursuant to section 215(d)(5) of the FPA, the ERO must affirmatively respond — it has discretion in how to respond but not in whether to respond.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If dissatisfied with a directive, parties may seek rehearing or judicial review, but once final the ERO must comply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on using stakeholder balloting to thwart directives
rubrics_metrics.description: Stakeholder balloting that delays indefinitely or 'ballots down' a responsive standard is improper if it prevents compliance with a Commission directive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FERC criticized 'misuse' of standards process that thwarts Congress’s goal in enacting section 215; the standards process cannot be used to avoid responding to directives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Due weight for ERO technical expertise
rubrics_metrics.description: FERC gives 'due weight' to the technical expertise of the ERO only when the ERO adequately explains the 'reliability benefits and technical considerations' of a proposed standard.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Due weight is not an abstract presumption; absent an adequate explanation in the record, there is nothing for the Commission to give due weight to (cites Order No. 740, Order No. 733).

rubrics_metrics.name: Openness and balanced stakeholder process requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The ERO must develop standards through an open and balanced stakeholder process, but the statute does not mandate the ANSI-certified process specifically; openness allows flexibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FERC reiterated that an ANSI-certified process is one way to meet the openness requirement, not the only way.

rubrics_metrics.name: NERC Rules of Procedure §321 alternative actions when regular process fails
rubrics_metrics.description: If the regular Standards Development Process does not produce a draft Reliability Standard responsive to a Commission directive, the NERC Board may: remand a draft standard to the Standards Committee with instructions; convene a technical conference followed by a stakeholder vote requiring 60% approval; or direct the Standards Committee or NERC management to prepare a draft standard.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are explicit procedural actions available to ensure responsiveness to FERC directives (approved by FERC in 134 FERC ¶ 61,216).

rubrics_metrics.name: FERC judicious use of directives
rubrics_metrics.description: FERC will issue directives under section 215(d)(5) 'only when appropriate to carry out section 215.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FERC stated it takes seriously the responsibility to use directive authority judiciously, but will use it where necessary to address reliability gaps.

rubrics_metrics.name: FERC may approve standards but direct follow-up reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: FERC sometimes approves a proposed reliability standard but directs NERC to submit a report after the effective date to inform FERC regarding the efficacy of the standard.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Based on post-implementation reports, FERC may determine whether further directives or modifications are warranted (example: Order No. 777 and Order No. 835).

rubrics_metrics.name: Criteria for FERC-initiated (sua sponte) new standards
rubrics_metrics.description: FERC will sua sponte direct development of a new standard based on whether (1) the subject poses a significant threat to bulk-power system reliability and (2) the ERO will timely address the matter on its own.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Not often articulated in orders but inferred from examples (geomagnetic disturbances, physical security, supply-chain risk).

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards retirement criteria (unnecessary or redundant requirements)
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirements proposed for retirement should either (1) provide little protection for Bulk-Power System reliability or (2) be redundant with other aspects of the Reliability Standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FERC will approve retirement where removal 'would not result in a reliability gap' (Order No. 788, Order No. 873, Order No. 902).

rubrics_metrics.name: FERC remand obligation when part of a standard is disapproved
rubrics_metrics.description: Under FPA section 215(d)(4), if the Commission disapproves a reliability standard in whole or in part, it must remand the standard to the ERO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FERC remanded an entire standard when it was not persuaded by NERC’s rationale for retiring a provision (Order No. 873 example).

rubrics_metrics.name: Cold-weather preparedness plan requirements for generator owners
rubrics_metrics.description: Generator owners must develop cold weather preparedness plans that include freeze protection measures, annual inspections, training, identification of cold weather operating parameters, and communication of that data to transmission operators and others.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NERC’s first set of cold weather standards required these elements; later standards added CAPs (corrective action plans) when equipment could not meet parameters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corrective Action Plans (CAPs) for cold-weather and planning gaps
rubrics_metrics.description: When studies or assessments indicate equipment or systems cannot withstand extreme weather scenarios, entities must develop corrective action plans to mitigate the effects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FERC has required CAPs both for generator owners and transmission planning (Order No. 896); FERC also directed deadlines for completing CAP mitigation measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability and exemption limits for standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Exclusions from applicability (e.g., excluded generating units) should be the exception, not the rule; exemption provisions must have objective criteria and an authority to review declared exceptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FERC directed NERC to clarify vague applicability language and to replace open-ended self-declaration exemptions with objective tests and a review authority (EOP-012-3 proceedings).

rubrics_metrics.name: Implementation deadlines and timelines for corrective actions
rubrics_metrics.description: FERC may shorten proposed long implementation timeframes (e.g., reduce a proposed 60-month window) and requires an appropriate deadline for completing CAP mitigation measures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FERC criticized industry delays in weatherization and imposed stricter timelines to ensure timely mitigation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost-recovery considerations are out of scope for §215 standard approval
rubrics_metrics.description: FERC will generally find cost recovery concerns out of scope for a proceeding under FPA section 215, because section 215 focuses on whether a proposed Reliability Standard achieves a reliability objective rather than rate recovery.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parties retain the right to seek cost recovery in appropriate forums under FPA sections 205/206 or other mechanisms, but §215 proceedings do not decide cost recovery.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptable substantive scope of reliability standards (operation of existing facilities)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reliability Standards may include requirements for the operation of existing bulk-power system facilities (e.g., freeze protection measures) and such requirements do not necessarily mandate construction of new or expanded generating capacity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FERC rejected arguments that freeze protection requirements exceeded statutory definitions of 'reliability standard' and 'reliable operation' when they do not require new capacity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transmission planning must consider extreme weather scenarios
rubrics_metrics.description: When performing long-term transmission planning studies, planners must specifically consider extreme heat and cold weather scenarios and develop CAPs if the system cannot withstand those scenarios.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Order No. 896 required transmission planners to include extreme-weather scenarios and imposed an 18-month deadline for submitting standards; FERC provided detailed sub-directives on benchmarking, studies, and assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: FERC will not mandate specific mitigation measures
rubrics_metrics.description: When directing the development of standards or CAPs, FERC generally will not prescribe specific mitigation measures, leaving NERC/industry discretion to select appropriate remedies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FERC stressed flexibility — standards should address reliability gaps but need not dictate precise technical solutions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Process for coordination with retail regulatory authorities on CAPs
rubrics_metrics.description: FERC directed NERC to develop processes to facilitate interaction and coordination with applicable regulatory authorities or governing bodies responsible for retail electric service when implementing CAPs; entities must share CAPs and solicit feedback on local reliability impacts and cost considerations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This unusual directive seeks collaboration with retail regulators to consider local impacts and cost issues in CAP implementation (Order No. 896 P 152-165).

rubrics_metrics.name: Detailed sub-directives for planning standards (benchmarking, studies, assessment)
rubrics_metrics.description: FERC's planning orders (e.g., Order No. 896) can include numerous detailed 'sub-directives' on matters such as cold weather benchmarking, studies, and assessments that the ERO must address.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Orders may include many technical sub-directives beyond high-level mandates and expect NERC to implement them in subsequent standard development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inverter-based resource standards substantive areas
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards addressing inverter-based resources should cover data sharing, model validation, planning and operational studies, and performance requirements (e.g., ride-through performance limits).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Order No. 901 identified these four high-level concerns and imposed more than sixty directives specifying expected content; FERC set tranches/deadlines for responsive standards with expectation to have standards effective well before 2030.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of alternative NERC procedures to meet FERC deadlines
rubrics_metrics.description: The NERC Board may invoke alternative standards-development procedures (e.g., §321 authority) to meet FERC deadlines when normal stakeholder processes would not produce a timely draft.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NERC invoked §321 authority for inverter-based resource and cold-weather deadlines; Board intervention can include technical conferences and use of different balloting thresholds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balloting thresholds in expedited/alternative procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: In the technical conference/alternative path, NERC may use a 60% ballot-body approval threshold instead of the typical two-thirds supermajority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This lower threshold is part of the §321 procedural tools to produce responsive drafts under FERC-imposed deadlines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Justification requirement for retiring individual requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: When proposing to retire requirements within a Reliability Standard, NERC must provide sufficient justification for each retirement; failure to justify may lead FERC to disapprove and remand the entire standard.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FERC approved many retirements where NERC demonstrated no reliability gap, but remanded when rationale for a specific retirement was insufficient (Order No. 873 example).
